newsitem.title: HONG KONG: External invest in HK non-manufacturing sector up.
newsitem.headline: External invest in HK non-manufacturing sector up.

text.p: The stock of inward direct investments in the non-manufacturing sectors of Hong Kong totalled HK$487.3 billion ($62.88 billion) at the end of 1995, up six percent from the end of 1994, the government said on Wednesday.

Analysed by individual investor country/territory, the United Kingdom was the largest investor country, accounting for 29 percent of the total at the end of 1995, the Census and Statistics Department said.
China and Japan followed with 21 percent and 14 percent respectively, while the United States was fourth at 12 percent.
Analysed by business sector, banks and deposit-taking companies attracted the largest share at 40 percent, while holding companies accounted for 22 percent.
Looking at manufacturing and non-manufacturing sectors taken together, the stock of inward direct investments amounted to HK$532.6 billion at the end of 1995, up seven percent from the end of 1994.
The share of the manufacturing sector in the overall total was around nine percent.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441 ($ = 7.749 Hong Kong Dollars)
